item.title: How America's Most Hated Airline Died | The Spirit Airlines Collapse
item.description:
At 3 a.m. on May 2, 2026, Spirit Airlines stopped flying for good. For most of its life the bright yellow budget airline was the most complained-about carrier in America, and also one of the most profitable. So how did it end in liquidation after 34 years?
It didn't die from one mistake. It took five blows: the big airlines copied its best idea, regulators blocked its rescue, an engine flaw grounded its planes, debt piled up, and a fuel shock finished it off.

item.title: How Saks Fifth Avenue Went Bankrupt | The $2.7 Billion Mistake
item.description:
In January 2026, the company behind Saks Fifth Avenue, Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman filed for bankruptcy, owing Chanel alone about $136 million. A 159-year-old luxury icon was brought down by a single deal that was supposed to save it.
This is how the $2.7 billion Neiman Marcus merger, a mountain of debt and a vicious cycle of unpaid suppliers and empty shelves turned Saks Global into one of the biggest retail collapses of the decade.
